title: partial-field-markers: NDJSON continuation and graceful schema-downgrade for truncated streaming outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When long structured outputs are streamed (chat-completions or function call responses) we currently either (a) cut off mid-token/object which causes parsers to fail, or (b) fall back to plain text which loses structured semantics. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight, backwards-compatible wire-level approach that makes truncated streaming outputs parseable and allows best-effort reconstruction across tool/function-call boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: New streaming payload mode 'ndjson-cont' can be requested via request header X-Redwood-Stream-Mode=ndjson-cont

A partial object split mid-field should include a per-field continuation marker ("partial_field": true) and an encoded continuation id so downstream parsers can either request the remainder or mark field as truncated without parse error
Existing clients that do not set X-Redwood-Stream-Mode continue to receive current behavior unchanged
Tool/function-calling handshake updated so the caller and callee can negotiate support for ndjson-cont; unsupported tool integrations degrade to current safe fallback
Unit + integration tests cover truncation at: UTF-8 byte boundary, escape sequence boundary, and nested array/object boundary
Performance overhead < 3% p95 token latency for typical 2k token responses when ndjson-cont enabled (bench on runtime-1.29)
Documentation and SDK helper parsers (JS/Py) published with examples for tolerant parsing and retry semantics
technical_notes: Wire format: stream lines are NDJSON objects. If a streaming chunk finishes and a JSON value is incomplete, emitter will send a minimal continuation object: { "__continuation": true, "cid": "<opaque-id>", "field_path": "choices[0].message.content.parts[2]", "partial_bytes_b64": "...", "partial_field": true }
Continuation id (cid) is a 128-bit random token encoded URL-safe base64; retained in ephemeral cache on sender side for 30s to support immediate resumption requests from proxies/clients

Partial bytes are base64 to preserve arbitrary bytes including multi-byte UTF-8 sequences—server guarantees we never cut inside a valid codepoint in the continuation payload (but may inside a logical token) and provides byte offsets

On tool/function boundaries, the runtime will emit a boundary object: { "__tool_boundary": true, "call_id": "...", "supported_modes": ["ndjson-cont"] } so adapters can route and optionally request completion from the upstream model before invoking a tool

SDK helper implements tolerant NDJSON parser: stitches contiguous non-boundary objects, converts continuation objects into 'truncated' flags on the nearest field, and exposes explicit 'resume' API to ask Redwood to provide the remainder for a cid
Avoids heavy-weight reassembly: goal is graceful degradation — produce syntactically valid JSON objects with 'truncated': true and 'truncated_hint' meta when full reconstruction unavailable
Backwards compatibility: default remains existing streaming JSON (single top-level JSON object emitted in chunks). ndjson-cont opt-in only.

Security: continuation cache must be forwarded only over authenticated control plane channels; callers without appropriate auth will not be allowed resume operations. No PII is stored longer than 30s. See security checklist.
decisions: Opt-in header vs protocol version bump: chosen to be an opt-in header (X-Redwood-Stream-Mode) to minimize client upgrade friction
Use NDJSON lines vs custom envelope: NDJSON chosen for simplicity with existing streaming parsers and to ease partial-line handling
Per-field partial markers instead of per-object checksums to make partial semantics explicit and enable partial-field presentation in clients
No long-term storage for continuation payloads; ephemeral 30s cache only (trade-off: simpler infra and privacy vs. limited time to resume)
tasks: Runtime: implement ndjson line emitter and CID tracking (Marco)
SDKs: JS and Python tolerant parsers + resume helper (R&D: Lina, Ben)
Console: show 'truncated' badges and a 'request completion' action when available (Design: Priya)
Tool adapters: add support in python-tool-adapter to respect boundary objects and request resume if adapter supports (SRE: Kofi)
Testing: fuzz tests for UTF-8, escape sequences, and nested arrays (QA: Taylor)
Docs: write developer guide + migration notes (Doc: Hazel)
testing_plan: Unit tests for emitter: verify NDJSON semantics and correct CID lifecycle
Integration: run against runtime-1.29 nightly with representative models (2B/13B) and measure p95 latency and memory
Fuzz harness: input model outputs with adversarial escapes and ensure parsers never throw (JS/Py SDKs)
End-to-end: simulate toolcall chains where model output is truncated mid-field and verify the callee and caller can agree to resume or render truncated hints
Canary: enable ndjson-cont for 1% of traffic and monitor parse errors, resume latency, and 'request completion' success rate
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'ndjson_cont_enabled' in runtime-1.29
SDK release: publish 0.8.0-js and 1.4.0-py with helpers; apps can opt-in by setting header
Canary: start with internal customers and Redwood-hosted beta customers
Monitor technical metrics and customer feedback for 2 weeks before wider rollout
Fallback: if p95 latency regresses >5% or resume error rate >1% revert flag and roll back SDK guidance
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha: Spiked two emitter variants. The NDJSON approach keeps parsers simple and lets us attach small continuation objects without changing base-line streaming for old clients.

2026-03-11 Marco: Implemented CID generator + ephemeral cache skeleton. Need guidance on retention window from Security. Also noticed a potential race when a proxy buffers chunks — adding explicit boundary objects to help proxies route correctly.
2026-03-11 Priya (Design): UX proposal: In Console chat view, show a faint '...truncated' pill next to fields and a 'Resume' button when a resume is available. See mock in linked Confluence.
2026-03-12 Harpreet (Security): OK with 30s cache if we encrypt with ephemeral key and log only metadata. Recommend adding a telemetry flag to redact sensitive examples from resume attempts.
2026-03-12 QA Taylor: Will add fuzz cases for 4 bytes UTF-8 splits and for surrogate pairs. Timeline looks tight for cycle, may request 1 sprint extension if integration shows edge regressions.
2026-03-12 Ben (SDK): Prototype parser handles continuation objects by attaching truncated metadata to the nearest field; we should standardize field_path syntax (dot + array indexes).
